Subject: MAP workbench: shared toolkit + kickstart GDoc

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation, I wanted to get you a tidy starter pack so your team can run a short evaluation and align internal stakeholders quickly. I put together a lightweight "MAP workbench" (one-page action plan + 4-week technical acceptance timeline) and a companion slide skeleton for your execs.

What's included in the pack:
- A one-page MAP scaffold (owners, acceptance criteria, success metrics)
- Week-by-week pilot checklist (tech validation, sample prompts, privacy/retention checks)
- Stakeholder RACI and decision gates
- Slide skeleton for a 10-minute alignment to your board/ops

Quick ask: can you share who will own integration testing on your side and the ideal date for a 30-minute sync next week? I can loop in our Solutions Engineer if you want a short run-through of the MAP doc.

I've attached a stubbed GDoc and GSlides — the doc allows co-edit so we can draft the MAP in-line. Link and attachments below.

Jonas
Lead, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-Workbench-Template-v1.gdoc (Google Doc stub), weekbyweek-kickstart-slides-v1.gslides (Slide stub)

Links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cMAPworkbench-kickstart

Jonas / Ben —

Thanks for the ping — I pulled the GDoc and added a short tech checklist under the "Week 1" section (integration endpoints, sample data, test prompts, KV cache expectations). A few notes while I was in there:

1) Acceptance criteria: propose we keep it to 3 measurable gates so Pilgrim can make a fast decision:
   - Latency: p95 <= 450ms on their 2k prompt sample
   - Quality: top-5 completion accuracy on reference set >= 88%
   - Privacy: retention policy confirmed and sample audit log produced

2) Owners: we should list Pilgrim owners (Sara + Ahmed) and our SE (Ben) — I'm tagging suggested owners in the doc.

3) Slide skeleton: added a one-slide "Pilot success definition" and a second slide for risks/mitigations.

Ben — can you confirm availability for Tue 11/30 10:30am PT (Sara suggested 10–11) and whether you want me to add implementation notes for quantization/throughput testing?

Marissa
